raised.note: confirmed by two sources in the run; the URLs were not saved
raised.value: $40M Series B led by Catalio Capital Management, after a $14M Series A led by Left Lane Capital in 2023

entry.idea: Evvy sells an at-home test that reads a woman's vaginal microbiome, then connects her with a doctor for treatment, tackling health issues doctors have historically had few good tools to diagnose.
entry.lesson: Applying modern sequencing technology to a health area that has been underinvested in for a long time can create both a real medical improvement and a strong business.
entry.name: Evvy

growth.reason: It serves over 100,000 patients and partners with 3,000 practitioners, clear evidence of real scale.

market.reason: Vaginal and reproductive health affects a very large population, and it is an area long underserved by conventional medicine, a large and growing market.

tech.reason: Its clinically validated genetic sequencing test for the vaginal microbiome is real scientific work, though competitors with similar lab capabilities could develop comparable tests over time.

sources.title: Evvy raises $40M as it seeks to further women's health research with vaginal microbiome data | TechCrunch
Evvy, Precision Women's Health Startup focused on the Vaginal Microbiome, Announces $14M Series A

entry.twist: Its test is the only clinically validated one of its kind using advanced genetic sequencing (mNGS) of the vaginal microbiome from a single swab, rather than the older, more limited standard lab tests.
entry.who_pays: Patients pay directly for testing, treatment and membership plans, with some costs covering lab work and clinical oversight by affiliated providers.
entry.why_now: Women's health conditions like vaginal symptoms, fertility issues and UTIs have long been underdiagnosed, and better and cheaper genetic sequencing technology now makes a detailed at-home microbiome test possible.

mentions.snippet: Vaginal microbiome testing and data to advance women's health research; $40M Series B.
